decisions.issues: Minor: Nagoji has narrow white cuffs at both wrists that could be read as wrist wraps. They are tiny at this scale. The two figures are mid-size rather than small. Everything else matches: a laterite and earth bastion seen from below and to one side, red dust, the red conch standard and the white pennant with a diagonal line crossed by a curved line, and De Lannoy in the patched white coat with pale tied hair and no hat. Nagoji has his topknot, grey temples, moustache, clean chin, gold stud, chain and shoulder cloth, with no coat. The open sky at upper left takes both captions.

Minor issues. Two lit brass oil lamps sit oddly on the foreground parapet in daylight. A plain red flag with no conch flies from a different stretch of wall, which also has a small corner turret. The musket line fires across the riders' ground while the wooden targets stand off to the upper left. The field gun's rammer man stands close beside its muzzle smoke, though not in its line of fire. The beat reads clearly: the view is from the bastion; Maravar riders with red shoulder cloths wheel in pairs between posts; bare-chested Nair musketeers in white mundu fire a volley; and a field gun recoils with white smoke. There are no coats or uniforms and no text. The clear sky band at the top holds the caption.

Minor: here the white pennant is long and swallow-tailed, while panels 1, 3 and 5 show a shorter triangle. Its device is correct: a diagonal line crossed by a curved line. There is a small cluster of distant red tile-roofed houses at the lower right. The low angle up the staff against a hard blue sky works, with the red conch standard above the pennant. There is no text, and large open sky on both sides takes the caption and the off-panel balloon.

Minor: the two men stand on the wall behind the tooth, and the staff and standard sit on the bastion point ahead of them. In 1.1 and 1.3 they stood at the staff, but the tooth's point aiming outward over the drill ground matches the 1.5 script. The troops below stand in blocks in short white jackets with cross belts, not coats. Both men are seen from behind: De Lannoy in the patched, frayed white coat with pale hair tied in a black ribbon, and Nagoji with his topknot, grey temples, gold stud, bare shoulder, shoulder cloth, thin silver chain and moustache edge. The sky band along the top holds the balloon and the caption.

Minor: the heavy chief's eyes slide toward his neighbour rather than clearly toward the far end of the hall. Everything else matches: Nagoji has the topknot, thick moustache, clean chin, grey temples, silver chain, shoulder cloth and mundu, with no coat, no knife and no bandages. De Lannoy wears the patched, frayed white coat and his pale hair is tied back. The chiefs have no turbans, lamps have open wicks, and the upper wall and ceiling are clear for both balloons.

Minor only: the seated chiefs carry no sandal-paste or ash forehead marks (2.1 asks for these, including on the heavy older chief, here at far right), and Padmini is walking with her stick rather than seated among them. Otherwise clean. Padmini matches her sheet: black hair coiled at the nape with grey threading it, a gold ear stud and chain, a cream sari with a gold border in the old drape with no blouse, and the long stick. She turns her head, unhurried, toward the older chief on the right. Nagoji and De Lannoy are correctly out of frame. Same pillared laterite hall, with open-wick brass lamps and daylight from the open side. No painted text, balloons or anachronism, and her hands are sound. The two balloons can sit on the low-detail laterite wall and ceiling at upper centre-right, clear of all faces.

Minor: on the drill ground a few men wear white headcloths, and a few muskets stand upright with no hand on them. At this distance the effect is small. The principals are correct: Nagoji has the topknot, moustache, clean chin, grey temples, small gold stud, silver chain and shoulder cloth, with no coat. De Lannoy wears the worn, patched white coat and his pale hair is tied with a black ribbon. The musketeers wear white mundu and stand in a ragged line with gaps. Dusk sky is clear for the caption and the long speech.

Minor: De Lannoy leans on the parapet, eyes on the palace roofs, instead of a clear shrug. Nagoji, arms crossed, watches him sidelong. Both men match their sheets (Nagoji: topknot, moustache, clean chin, gold stud, silver chain, no coat; De Lannoy: patched white coat with frayed cuffs). The setting matches panel 2.3, and the dusk sky is clear for both short balloons.

Minor: at this scale Nagoji's gold ear ornament reads as a tiny bead and may hang slightly. Otherwise clean. The frame is a wide 3:1 strip. Both men stand on the rampart at the left, De Lannoy laughing in the patched white coat and Nagoji in topknot, mundu and chain. Below them the Kerala tiled roofline steps down to an audience hall with the throne platform. The broad dusk sky is clear for all three speeches.

Minor issues only. Nagoji's ear stud is a small flush stud but reads pale or pearl rather than gold. There is faint stubble shading on his jaw, but the chin reads clean. On the right wall map, a few tiny scribbles near De Lannoy's shoulder (about x 0.91-0.94, y 0.31-0.36) look letter-like at high zoom but read as map hatching at print size; the second Ramayyan balloon can sit over that map. Otherwise this is on script: war hall, timber pillars, laterite walls, unlit brass lamps, Ramayyan with palm-leaf bundle and stylus between the two men leaning on a plan of a wall. Nagoji has a topknot, grey temples, mundu, shoulder cloth, silver chain, no coat. De Lannoy wears the patched, frayed white coat. Clear roof and sky space at top left and top centre for the balloons.

Clean. The young bare-chested recruit in a hitched white mundu has just fired: smoke at his muzzle and a dust spurt short of and wide of the target. De Lannoy (pale hair tied back, bare-headed, worn white coat with patches and frayed cuffs, sandals) is walking toward him from behind the line, and the onlookers stand behind or beside it. The only flag is the red conch standard. There is wide sky at the top for the short 'Again.' balloon. This panel sets the recruit's look for the page: bare-chested, curly hair, white mundu with a thin red border.

Acceptable with a continuity note. The recruit wears a white upper cloth draped over both shoulders, plus leather straps, where he is bare-chested in 3.2. His face and curly hair still carry the identity, and the beat (fumbling at a brass powder horn, sweating, anxious) reads clearly. Nagoji's ear ornament is a tiny gold bead set close to the lobe, acceptable as a stud. His silver chain is worn diagonally across the shoulder cloth. Nagoji has a topknot, grey temples, curled moustache and clean chin, and turns back on Kayal to call down. Kayal is a bay with black mane, tail and lower legs and no white. The firing line is seen side-on with Nagoji behind it. Open sky at the top right takes both Nagoji balloons.

Minor issues only. As in 3.1, Nagoji's ear stud reads pale or silver rather than gold. The Maravar riders wear white shoulder cloths with red waist cloths, not red shoulder cloths. The specific recruit is not singled out in the firing line. Otherwise on script: Nair musketeers in white mundu, no uniforms, fire a high volley in time over two cantering riders. De Lannoy (white coat, frayed cuffs, ribbon-tied pale hair) and Nagoji (topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, bare chest, silver chain, arms folded) stand at the left edge, beside and behind the line. Wide sky above both heads for the two balloons.

Only one candidate listed. v02 matches the beat: the boy is grinning, sweat runs down his face, and his musket is grounded with both hands folded over the muzzle. His look (bare-chested, white mundu with red border, powder horn on a strap) matches the youth in 3.2/3.3, and the firing line behind is side-on in white mundus, consistent with 3.4. The drill ground, laterite bastion, field gun, wooden targets and red conch standard match the setting. There is no painted text and no balloons. Minor issues: the boy rests his hands on the muzzle, which is unsafe handling but reads naturally. The arched whitewashed armoury at left looks faintly colonial, but it is plausible as a fort building. The open blue sky in the upper right gives clear space for the short recruit balloon and the medium caption without covering faces or hands.

Minor only. Ibrahim's ear-to-jaw scar is on the correct (anatomical left) side but reads slightly reddish rather than pale. Nagoji's inner-left-forearm scar is hidden by his crossed arms. Otherwise clean: Nagoji has the topknot, grey temples, thick moustache, clean chin, flush gold stud, silver chain and no coat or knife. Ibrahim has the white turban, grey-flecked beard, teal short coat, pocketed vest and a toddy cup. Padmini has black hair with grey threads coiled at the nape, a cream gold-bordered sari with no blouse and the stick across her knees. The scene is a lamplit laterite verandah with an open-wick brass lamp, and there is no text. Lettering space: the roof rafters at upper centre for Ibrahim and the plain wall at upper right for Padmini.

Minor only. The distant fort through the gate is a small hilltop castle rather than an angled bastion point. The low table has turned legs. Nagoji's grey at the temples is heavier than first grey, but it matches the other panels. The beat is right: Revathi is reading palm leaves without looking up, the steward is beside her, the brass grain measure is at hand and Nagoji stands before her. Both characters match their sheets. There is no text, and a large clear sky at upper centre holds both balloons.

Minor only. The camera has moved to the opposite side from 4.2 (Nagoji now left, steward right). Two small distant hilltop forts show, one above the roofline and one through the gate. Revathi's braid falls on the other shoulder. The beat reads clearly: she hands a bundle to the steward without looking at it, her eyes on Nagoji, and Nagoji has crossed arms and a sceptical raised brow. He is clean-shaven with a flush gold stud. There is no text, and the upper roof and sky give room for both balloons.

v03 is the newest version and it is acceptable. It shows the beat: Revathi standing, the old steward carrying the palm-leaf bundles away towards the house, Revathi looking right past Nagoji towards the open south gate, and the distant grey fort above the palms. It is the same sunlit courtyard, gate and hill fort as 4.2, 4.3 and 4.5. Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch24 1-14.1 row: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold stud, grey at the temples, topknot, silver chain, white mundu and shoulder cloth, no knife and no coat. There is no painted text, and there is a large clear sky area at upper right for Revathi's balloon. Minor faults left: (1) Revathi's sandalwood line at the hairline and the grey threads in her hair cannot be seen at this size, and her necklace is gold beads rather than flat coins (this matches her sheet). (2) Nagoji's mundu is plain white, without the gold kasavu border it has in 4.2, 4.3 and 4.5. (3) The table is a taller carved bench rather than the low table in the neighbouring panels. (4) The bastion is drawn as a generic hill-fort outline, not a clear angled bastion point, and it appears twice: once above the roofline and again through the gate. (5) Nagoji's inner left forearm brand and scar are not visible from this angle, which is acceptable here. Rejected: v01 has Revathi still seated and no steward leaving, which misses the beat. v02 has a white-handled knife hilt tucked into Nagoji's mundu at the waist, which breaks the no-knife rule.
decisions.correction: No retouch is needed to use v03. If the author wants the doubled fort fixed, there is a small optional local retouch: paint out the upper fort outline above the roofline (about x 1170-1345, y 248-292 px in the 1536x1024 frame) with the surrounding palms and sky, so only the small grey fort seen through the gate remains.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Nagoji now sits on the mat across the low table, where he stood in 4.2 to 4.4, which is plausible for a closer two-shot. A small brass lamp is lit in daylight. The beat is right: a two-shot, Revathi's hand flat on the stack of palm leaves, and she is not smiling. Both characters match their sheets; Nagoji has a clean-shaven chin and a flush gold stud. There is no text, and the sky at upper right and the wall and roof at upper left give room for three short balloons.

Acceptable and fixes every r1 failure. Varma has black hair in a knot on his left side, the namam and pearl earrings from his sheet, and gold necklaces. He holds the plain brass-buttoned coat high like a trophy. Nagoji is nearest the camera and lit, and matches his sheet: topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, small gold stud, silver chain, white mundu and shoulder cloth, and the healed brand and scar on his inner left forearm with no letters. De Lannoy stands apart by the maps in his patched white coat with pale hair tied back. Nair, Maravar and Madurai officers are all present. Minor points: a small brass cross-shaped rule or instrument lies on the table; the wall lights are candle-like open flames; and Varma's back-of-shoulder bandage cannot be seen from the front. The wall maps carry plain lines and small building pictograms, with no text. The upper-left wall and ceiling band is free for the caption, and the band above Varma's head is free for his balloon.

Acceptable and fixes the r1 maker's label. The insert shows the long white European-cut coat with one column of plain polished brass buttons catching the lamplight, plain cuffs with brass cuff buttons and no label. Beside it lie the red waistcoat, folded knee breeches, white stockings and black buckled shoes. It is on the map table with open-wick brass lamps and the latticed night window. Minor: the margin of the right-hand wall map, at the frame edge, carries tiny illegible tick marks and a speck of scrawl. This is the same kind of map scribble already accepted, and it is not readable at panel size. There is no lettering in this panel.

Minor only. The moustache is a little heavier than the bible's 'thin, neatly waxed' wording, but it matches the V15 sheet. The bandage sits at the front and top of his LEFT shoulder rather than at the back. The wall sconces are brass open-flame sconces, which is acceptable. The upper wall areas behind the balloons (a map on the left, the lattice window and a map on the right) are mid-detail, not blank, but they hold two medium balloons without covering the face or hands. Everything else is right: the face, namam, pearl drops and the side knot above the LEFT ear all match the sheet; he is bare-headed and bare-chested in a cream mundu with gold necklaces; his right hand lies flat on a plain white coat with a single column of plain brass buttons, matching 5.2; the red waistcoat is beside it; the maps carry no lettering; the hands are sound. v02 is the backup but is weaker: its coat has gold trim and a double button row, which does not match the plain coat in 5.2. v01 is out: no coat, loose wavy hair, no namam.

Acceptable. The heavy, grey older Nair captain has white ash stripes, a topknot and no coat. He leans on the table with his hand at his chin, which reads as careful and hesitant. It is the same laterite and timber hall with brass lamps, unlettered maps and the latticed window. His hands are sound and there is no text. Minor: no other officers are visible behind him, and his fist partly covers his mouth. The dark upper-centre wall and the upper-left wall give clean room for both balloons.

Acceptable and fixes the r1 failure. Varma leans over the table toward the room with both palms planted on the white brass-buttoned coat, in a wide 3:1 strip with his face in the middle band. His look matches: black hair in a side knot on his left, the namam, pearl earrings, gold necklaces, the white bandage over his left shoulder, a bare chest and a cream mundu with gold border. His hands are sound. The laterite and timber hall has open-wick brass lamps, spear racks and the latticed window. Minor points: the coat cuff has a thin gold edge line; the left wall map carries a few tiny illegible scribble labels, the kind already accepted; and the window looks out onto a lamplit fort wall. The wall and roof areas either side of his head, upper left and upper right, are clear for both balloons.

Minor only. Varma's hair knot sits on the crown and not clearly above the left ear. Everything else matches. De Lannoy has pale hair tied back with a black ribbon, a worn white coat with patched elbows and frayed cuffs, and pale hands on the map with dividers. Varma is bare-headed and bare-chested, with gold necklaces, a gold-bordered cream mundu and a white cloth on his left shoulder, and he looks toward De Lannoy. The war hall has laterite walls, a tiled roof, open-wick brass lamps and a latticed window. Hands are sound and the maps carry no text. The roof beams across the top leave room for the balloon.

Minor. The background officers have no sandal-paste or ash forehead marks. One moustached officer at left (hand on chin, thin gold chain) faintly resembles Nagoji, but he has no silver chain of office and no topknot, so he reads as a generic officer. De Lannoy matches his sheet and the bible: pale hair tied with a ribbon, bare-headed, worn white coat with elbow patches and frayed cuffs. He leans in at the table with the room's eyes on him. Only he wears a coat, the maps carry no text and the hands are sound. The roof and the upper walls (top left and top right) leave room for two balloons.

Minor. Varma's hair knot sits low at the nape, not above the left ear, so it is placed differently from 6.1. The shoulder bandage wraps the front of his left shoulder. Otherwise it matches the sheet: bare-headed and bare-chested, gold necklaces, pearl earring, gold-bordered cream mundu, leaning over the map table and pointing. The same laterite war hall as 6.1 and 6.2, with open-wick lamps and a latticed window. The maps show only lines and pictograms, no text, and the hands are sound. The roof and upper wall at right (and the upper left) leave room for two balloons.

Accepted with moderate deviations. (1) The three other officers also wear silver link chains, which weakens the script note that Nagoji is the only officer with a chain of office. He still stands out: he is centred and lit, younger, clean-shaven, with no forehead mark, while the others are grey, bearded and marked. (2) No visible first grey at Nagoji's temples. (3) His hair is a loose curly mass with a knot on the crown, not fully bound in a Kerala topknot. (4) He is centred and lit, not the figure nearest the camera; a foreground officer at the right edge is nearer. (5) The back wall reads as grey stone, not the laterite of 6.1 to 6.3. Nagoji's constants are right: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold stud, no forehead mark, white mundu and shoulder cloth, bare arms, no coat, knife or bandages. He looks down at the coat (plain brass buttons, red waistcoat), and the older marked officers watch. Hands are sound and there is no text. Two short captions fit over the wall between the left officers' heads and Nagoji (upper left of centre) and over the roof beams at upper right.

Minor. The gaol guards wear tall boots, not buckled shoes. The frame cuts the Goa officer just below the nose, so his lips and jaw show, not a cut at the chin; his eyes are never shown, which is the key rule. The scene is in fairly full colour, but the edges bleed into a ragged stain as asked. Everything else matches: wet vaulted stone corridor; two white-coated Portuguese soldiers with red cuffs and black tricornes walking away far down it; the officer's queue under a black tricorne, gilt-laced white coat, ornate gilt buttons, red waistcoat and sword at the hip, adjusting a cuff; guards in morions, off-white shirts and buff jerkins with nothing red or blue. Keshavrao looks back: young, faint moustache, short hacked hair, grey-brown torn tunic. Nagoji is seen from behind in a torn ochre sleeveless tunic and cream dhoti, with bandaged wrists, ankle irons, bare feet and loose curly hair. Empty manacles hang from a ring in the cell, with no noose, blood or text. The stone wall above the group at upper left and centre leaves room for the caption.

Minor only. The framing is head and shoulders rather than tight on the throat and jaw. The crown is cropped at the frame top, so no topknot reads (the hair looks loose with a thin band). The faint memory-bleed stain at the panel edge is not drawn. Nagoji matches his sheet and bible row: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, flush gold ear stud, grey at the temples, silver chain, shoulder cloth, no coat. The upper-left roof and upper-right wall are clear for the two captions.

Clean. Varma matches his sheet: sleek black hair with the side knot above the LEFT ear, namam, pearl drops, upturned moustache, bare-chested in a gold-bordered cream mundu with gold beads, and a clean cloth bandage on the LEFT shoulder. The war hall is right (laterite walls, timber pillars, latticed night window, maps with no lettering, open-wick brass lamps). Hands are sound. The upper-left wall map and the ceiling at upper right leave room for the balloon and the caption. The white coat is not on the table here, but the script does not ask for it in this panel.

Acceptable, with minor notes. The two-shot works: the folded white coat with brass buttons and red lining lies between them. Nagoji is correct: topknot, grey at the temple, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small flush gold stud, silver chain, white mundu and shoulder cloth, no coat. The brand is on his LEFT forearm. Varma is correct: left side knot, namam, pearl drops. Notes: Varma's LEFT-shoulder bandage is not visible because his gold-bordered cloth covers that shoulder; he wears an upper-arm armlet; Nagoji's scar line runs a little way up the upper arm; Nagoji's gesture is a touch more animated than 'level'. The balloons can sit on the roof timbers and upper wall along the top band.

v03 is clean and shows the beat: over Nagoji's bare shoulder (topknot, grey at the temple, thick moustache, small gold stud, silver chain, white shoulder cloth, no coat) onto bare-headed Varma (side knot above his left ear, namam, pearl drops, thin waxed moustache, gold necklaces, cream mundu with gold border), with the folded white coat and its plain brass buttons in the foreground. No text, hands look sound. Small faults: Varma's bandage at the back of his left shoulder can't be seen from the front, though the wrapped shoulder cloth on that shoulder could pass for it. Nagoji's chin is turned away, so the clean-shaven chin can't be checked here, but nothing contradicts it. The upper band where the balloons go (roof beams, plain-line wall maps) is a little busy but usable: put the balloons over the upper-left wall map between Nagoji's head and the pillar, and over the roof and upper wall above Varma. v02 is the same image except for a puckered scar on Nagoji's RIGHT forearm, the wrong arm, which v03 removes. v01 is rejected because Nagoji wears the new white coat, which nobody wears in this room.

Minor only. Varma's hair is a crown topknot with loose curls rather than a side knot above his LEFT ear, and his shoulder bandage is not visible (the back of his shoulder is turned away). The officers are somewhat alike. The beat reads well: Varma gesturing as he addresses the room, officers with forehead marks turning for the door, and Nagoji standing still at the right as the only man with the silver chain and no forehead mark (clean-shaven chin, moustache, flush gold stud, grey temples, topknot, no coat). The roof beams across the top centre give clear space for both of Varma's balloons.

Clean. Nagoji matches the sheet and bible row: topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, tiny gold stud, silver chain, white mundu and shoulder cloth, no coat. Varma has the namam, pearl drops, his left-side knot and the bandaged left shoulder, and keeps his eyes on the folded white coat. The wall maps are plain and unlettered. The roof timbers top centre and top right give room for both balloons.

Acceptable. Varma matches his sheet and holds the plain white coat (brass buttons, red lining, no facings or stains) at arm's length with his bandaged left arm. Two small continuity drifts: an unrolled map and a brass pen-pot now sit on the table, which was bare in panel 1, and the window bars are a square grid instead of panel 1's diamond lattice. The wall maps carry no lettering. The upper-left map wall and the roof at top right are clear for both balloons.

v02 is the least-bad of the three. The beat works: the fingers stop just above a plain brass button on the white coat, which has a red waistcoat and lining. The face is softly out of focus behind the hand. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small flush gold ear studs, topknot, grey at the temples, silver chain. The room fits too: night war hall, open-wick brass lamps, latticed window, a map with plain lines. There is no text or pseudo-text, and the brand reads as scar tissue, not letters. Remaining faults: (1) The arm is mirrored. The reaching arm comes from his right shoulder, on the left of the frame, so the brand and scar are on the back of his RIGHT forearm. The script and bible put them on the inner LEFT wrist. (2) His shoulder cloth wraps both shoulders like a sleeveless vest, so his chest is covered. Panels 8.1, 8.2, 8.4 and 8.5 show it over one shoulder with the chest bare. This is a small costume mismatch. (3) The thumb is hidden under the hand. That is plausible but leaves only four fingers visible. Lettering: put the single NAGOJI balloon on the dark upper-right wall above the map (about x 0.65 to 0.95, y 0.03 to 0.20), clear of the face and hand. Why not the others: v03, the newest, has one arm with two hands (a second hand grows out of the top of the scarred forearm, which then carries on into a palm-up hand at bottom right). v01 has no coat at all; the finger touches a map counter, and his hair is long and loose with no topknot.
decisions.correction: No small local pixel retouch fixes the worst fault, the brand on the wrong arm. The art has no lettering, so a full horizontal flip of the frame is safe. The flip would make the reaching arm his LEFT arm and keep the face, coat and balloon space usable. The brand would still sit on the back of the forearm rather than the inner wrist. If the brand's side matters more than the composition, flip the frame. Otherwise accept it as is.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. Varma matches his sheet: namam, pearl drops, thin upturned moustache, sleek knot on his left side, bandage on his left shoulder. He sets the same plain white coat (brass buttons, turned-back cuff, red waistcoat beneath) on the near side of the table. The hall matches panels 1 and 2. Minor: two tiny, unreadable letter-like specks on the lower margin of the left wall map, at about x 0.04 to 0.12 and y 0.35 to 0.41. They are about 15 px wide and could be covered by a balloon placed over that map. The upper-left map wall and the roof timbers at top right are clear for both balloons.

Acceptable. Full-width strip: Varma stands at the latticed window at right with his back to the room and night outside, the bandage on his left shoulder. Nagoji is alone at the table on the left, bare-chested with the shoulder cloth, silver chain, topknot, grey temples, thick moustache, clean chin and gold stud, with both hands on the table over the folded white coat. Minor drifts: the walls are dull plaster instead of the red laterite of panels 1, 2 and 4. In this back view Varma's hair coil sits on his right side rather than his left, which is subtle at this scale. There are tiny unreadable specks along the bottom margin of the left wall map. The plain wall between the pillars (x 0.45 to 0.72, upper half) and the roof timbers give clear space for both balloons.

Minor only. The small pennant is drawn as a straight blue saltire rather than a diagonal crossed by a curved line. It is drawn the same way in panels 2 to 4, so the page stays consistent. De Lannoy's head is turned to profile, a glance aside rather than strictly 'not turning', but his body stays at the parapet facing out. Nagoji's left-forearm scars show as two thin crossing pale lines instead of a puckered brand patch with one long scar. They are small at reading size. The drill men are bare-chested with staves, while in panel 2 they wear white tunics and carry muskets. The sea is more prominent than 'a distant line'. Otherwise correct: Nagoji climbs the last steps with his topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, silver chain, mundu and shoulder cloth, and no coat or knife. De Lannoy wears the patched, frayed white coat and holds a brass cup. The scene is a laterite bastion at sunset with copper drill ground below, and there is ample open sky in the top left and top centre for three balloons.

Minor only. The camera is over the shoulder and slightly high, not a true low angle along the parapet. The drill men wear white tunics with red sashes and carry muskets, and two instructors wear dark blue sleeveless vests. That differs from the bare-chested men with staves in panel 1, but they are small background figures. The pennant is a straight saltire (same as the rest of the page). The beat is clear: De Lannoy turns the brass cup in freckled pale hands, eyes on the drill below, sun low behind the far hills. His coat is patched and frayed and his hair is tied with a black ribbon. Open sky to the right of his head and across the top has room for two balloons.

Minor only. Nagoji's ear studs are small round gold balls on both lobes. They are still studs, nothing hangs from them. His topknot has a thin gold band. The pennant is a straight saltire (same as the rest of the page). The beat is clear: De Lannoy laughs softly with eyes lowered, cup raised near his mouth, and Nagoji leans on the parapet at his shoulder watching him. Nagoji's thick curled moustache, clean chin, grey temples, silver chain, shoulder cloth and bare arms all match. Clean sky across the top and to the right of Nagoji's head has room for three balloons. The hands are sound.

Minor only. The pennant is a straight X (saltire) rather than a diagonal crossed by a curved line, but it matches panels 9.1 to 9.3. The cup is a straight brass beaker where the neighbouring panels show a goblet. The hair is a slightly darker ash blond than in 9.1 to 9.3. Otherwise clean. De Lannoy matches his sheet: pale hair tied back with a black ribbon, bare-headed, worn white coat patched at the elbow with frayed cuffs. He faces off-frame toward Nagoji with the sunset behind him on the same laterite bastion. There is no painted text, and the hand on the cup is sound.
